notes: Metallus is the public specialty steel maker (NYSE: MTUS) formerly named TimkenSteel; its 10-K for the year ended Dec. 31, 2024 reports about 1,880 employees, an Ohio state of incorporation and headquarters at 1835 Dueber Avenue SW in Canton. The EIN on the 990 matches the EIN in the 10-K exactly. JobsOhio's July 2024 report lists a $3.0 million Economic Development Grant and a $500,000 Workforce Grant for a $112.7 million Stark County project with 1,602 jobs retained; the company was created in Ohio in 2014 as a spinoff of Canton-based Timken.

parent: Miami University (State of Ohio public university)
notes: The $1.5 million is a JobsOhio Vibrant Community Grant for the Lee and Rosemary Fisher Innovation College@Elm, a 39,000-square-foot incubator in Oxford built with the City of Oxford and The Fischer Group. The Ohio Department of Development's Major Employers report ranks Miami University 73rd in the state with 4,442 Ohio employees; the university was founded in Oxford in 1809.

Cenovus Energy's 2024 Annual Information Form, filed with its Form 40-F, lists Husky Marketing and Supply Company as a wholly owned Delaware material subsidiary and reports 7,150 full-time-equivalent employees at Dec. 31, 2024; Cenovus is headquartered in Calgary, Alberta. The Dublin, Ohio address is the US regional office; JobsOhio's July 2024 report shows a $4.0 million Workforce Grant against a $1.44 billion investment at the Lima and Toledo refineries, with 942 jobs retained.

MedShip is an operating distributor of surgical dressings, not a developer: the $750,000 Vibrant Community Grant paid for its own 12,000-square-foot headquarters in downtown Camden, which it built after demolishing two blighted buildings and into which it invested $2.3 million of its own money. Its COO says 86 of the company's 93 employees work in Camden, and JobsOhio calls MedShip an Ohio-grown startup less than four years old.

The Crescent-News reports that local businessman Bryan Keller and his partners have spent more than three years redeveloping the 1874 building at 300 Clinton St. in downtown Defiance, finishing the second floor as 11 offices to rent by the hour, day, week or year, the third floor as office space, and the first floor for a restaurant tenant it is still trying to sign. Owning and leasing that space to others is the LLC's whole business, so it is site development; no JobsOhio release or project-metrics row was found for the $511,413.

Not a project LLC: King's Command Foods (2022), LLC runs a federally inspected prepared-foods plant at 770 N. Center St. in Versailles, and the $425,000 Economic Development Grant backed a $20.4 million expansion of that plant with 150 jobs retained and 60 created, so it is classed as a business. The Sidney Daily News reported in 2016 that the cooking operations are based in Kent, Washington, with another plant in Oklahoma City, and that the business had combined with American Prepared Foods Group of Green Bay, Wisconsin. I could not confirm who owns it after the 2022 change the entity name implies, and no worldwide employee figure was found, so the bucket is an inference from the three-plant footprint; graded D.

EPC is an injection molder founded in 1994 by Reza Kargarzadeh, who still owns and runs it; the JobsOhio release describes more than 14 facilities in ten states and Mexico, over 200 molding machines, and 200-plus employees at one plant alone, which is why the bucket is 500-4999 rather than a counted figure. The 990 address is Grinnell, Iowa; JobsOhio's January 2025 report shows a $350,000 Economic Development Grant for a $9 million Huron County project with 180 jobs retained.

Battle Motors builds refuse and vocational trucks at the former Crane Carrier plant in New Philadelphia, which Wikipedia records it bought in 2021 and which Crane Carrier's founder Robert Zeligson started in 1946. JobsOhio's February 2025 report lists 591 jobs retained and 309 created in Tuscarawas County against a $21.9 million investment, so the Ohio site alone is over 500; the company reported layoffs in New Philadelphia in early 2025, so the figure may have fallen.

This is a spec-building grant, not a company expansion: the $360,000 came through the Ohio Site Inventory Program for a 30,000-square-foot speculative industrial and office building in the Salt Creek Industrial Park in Jackson County, built to attract tenants that have not been named. JobsOhio's own report lists the jobs, industry and investment as TBD. No separate developer or employee count was named, so the LLC is treated as its own parent.

Haag-Streit's own site says the Haag-Streit Group was integrated into Metall Zug AG as its medical devices business unit in 2018, and Metall Zug's site says the holding company is based in Zug, Switzerland and employs about 900 people worldwide. Haag-Streit USA in Mason is the group's US sales and service arm; JobsOhio's August 2024 report shows a $200,000 Economic Development Grant for a $4.9 million Warren County project with 114 jobs retained.

Classed as a business rather than site development because warehousing is what Pinnacle sells: OhioSE describes it and its affiliate Trinity Real Estate USA, LLC, both run by president John Jack, as providing warehousing, repackaging and transportation from an ISO-certified plant. The $160,000 Revitalization Grant paid to bring the former Mahle Engine building in Caldwell, vacant since 2009, back into use for Pinnacle's own operations; JobsOhio lists 21 jobs retained and 13 created.

Safecor Health repackages unit-dose drugs for more than 1,000 hospitals and has had its headquarters in Columbus since 2011, though it was founded in 2008; the $150,000 Workforce Grant supported a Franklin County expansion with 129 jobs retained and 100 created. Google News indexes a PR Newswire release on an August 2021 recapitalization by Vesey Street Capital Partners, a New York health-care private-equity firm; under the method the operating company, not the fund, is the parent.

JobsOhio's November 2023 report lists a $125,000 Economic Development Grant for a $1.25 million Franklin County project with 41 jobs retained and 17 created, which makes it an operating business of under 100 people at the Gahanna address on the 990. I could not establish what RTeam Management does or whether it has a parent: there is no JobsOhio release, no Form 5500 or SEC record for the EIN, no website I could find, and the similarly named RTEAM is a Jacksonville, Florida events firm, not this company. Graded D.

Treated as a business, not site development: the $100,000 Revitalization Grant went to an operating manufacturer putting a building back to work for itself, and JobsOhio lists 28 jobs retained and 20 created across Lorain and Medina counties on a $1.5 million investment. Google News indexes a 2013 PlasticsToday article on Castek building one of North America's largest aluminum thermoform molds, which I could not fetch; castek.com is a parked domain for sale, and I found no sign of a corporate parent.

JobsOhio calls Mira an Ohio-based, privately held precision-medicine company founded in 2020 that runs molecular diagnostic testing through independent pharmacies and primary-care practices, and the grant tripled the size of its Mason lab. The July 2024 report shows a $100,000 Economic Development Grant for an $810,500 Warren County project with 12 jobs retained and 29 created.

JobsOhio's December 2023 report lists a $100,000 Economic Development Grant in the energy and chemicals sector for a $744,064 Franklin County project with 17 jobs retained and 32 created. The 990's 43085 zip is Worthington, which matches Columbus Business First and WSYX headlines from November 2023 about veteran business partners expanding Worthington manufacturing into a 120,000-square-foot facility; both stories are behind a paywall or script-rendered and I could not fetch either, so the call rests on JobsOhio's own report.

IE Corp is a family-owned maker of switchgear and power infrastructure founded in 1985 and based in Price, Utah, with plants there, in South Point, Ohio and in Centralia, Illinois. ETV News reported in late 2026 that its workforce had grown from just under 300 in 2023 to about 620, which places it in the 100-499 range during the 2024-25 grant year, though it may have crossed 500 by then. JobsOhio's July 2024 report shows a $75,000 Economic Development Grant for a $12 million Lawrence County expansion with 62 jobs retained.

Westrafo America LLC is the US arm of a privately held Italian power-transformer maker whose other plants are in Vicenza, Italy and Tema, Ghana; the Trotwood plant opened in October 2025 on a $15 million initial investment. JobsOhio's October 2024 report shows a $1 million Economic Development Grant for 230 new jobs and no jobs retained, of which $71,995 was paid in FY2025. No group employee figure was published, so the bucket is inferred from three production sites and the company's statement that it has more than doubled in size since 2021.

JobsOhio's May 2024 report lists a $50,000 Small Business Grant in advanced manufacturing for a $106,650 Greene County project creating two jobs; the Small Business Grant is restricted to companies that meet JobsOhio's size limits. The 990 address is Beavercreek. No website, release or news coverage was found, so nothing indicates a parent company.

Battle Sight Technologies' own site describes tactical products developed and field-tested by warfighters for warfighters, including a power-management technology; the 990 address is downtown Dayton. JobsOhio's December 2023 report lists a $50,000 Inclusion Grant, which is capped at $50,000 and limited to small businesses, for a $100,327 Montgomery County project with five jobs retained and one created.

JobsOhio's January 2022 report lists a $50,000 Inclusion Grant in food and agribusiness for a $230,000 Ross County project with three jobs retained and two created, which places the company well under 100 employees. No website or news coverage was found, so I could not confirm who owns it; nothing suggests a parent.

Elliott Machine Works' own site markets telemanipulators and related equipment for the nuclear medicine and radiopharmaceutical industries. JobsOhio's April 2024 report lists a $50,000 Small Business Grant for a $3.16 million Crawford County project with 66 jobs retained and 15 created, so the Galion plant is the company's main operation and it is under 100 people.

A construction contractor builds for other people but does not own or lease the real estate, so this is a business rather than site development. JobsOhio's July 2023 report lists a $50,000 Inclusion Grant for a $125,000 Lorain County project with three jobs retained and nine created. A JobsOhio success story about a Lorain-area entrepreneur named Kameron turns out to be a different company, so I could not confirm the owner.

JobsOhio classes this as a logistics and distribution project and lists a $50,000 Small Business Grant with four jobs retained and two created in Cuyahoga County, which is why it is a business rather than site development. But the investment behind it is $2.2 million against four existing jobs, which leaves open that most of the money went into a building, and I found no website, release or news coverage for the Rocky River address, so neither the line of business nor any parent is confirmed. Graded D.

JobsOhio's January 2024 report lists a $50,000 Inclusion Grant in advanced manufacturing for a $2.95 million Columbiana County project with 21 jobs retained and five created. The 990 address is Salem. The company website returned no readable content, so the size and class rest on JobsOhio's own report and the small-business cap on the Inclusion Grant.

JobsOhio's April 2024 report lists a $50,000 Small Business Grant in advanced manufacturing for a $54,000 Summit County project with four jobs retained and three created, which is a company of a handful of people at the Akron address on the 990. No website or coverage was found and nothing suggests a parent.

JobsOhio's January 2024 report lists a $50,000 Inclusion Grant in food and agribusiness for a $292,000 project with two jobs retained and nine created; the report puts the project in Miami County while the 990 address is Bellefontaine in Logan County, a discrepancy I could not resolve. Either way this is a small food business, not a real-estate entity, and no parent company appeared in any source.

National Access Design's own site says the company is based in Cincinnati and manufactures industrial and commercial doors, including traffic, cold storage and dock products, in the United States. JobsOhio's October 2023 report lists a $35,000 Inclusion Grant for a $786,868 Hamilton County project with 10 jobs retained and two created.

JobsOhio's January 2024 report lists a $25,000 Inclusion Grant in the technology sector for a $35,000 Stark County project with one job retained and two created, so this is a very small Canton firm. I could not find a website or any coverage that identifies the owners, and nothing suggests a parent.

An excavating contractor sells site work to other people rather than owning or leasing real estate, so this is a business. JobsOhio's April 2025 report lists a $25,000 Small Business Grant for a $123,000 Paulding County project with five jobs retained and one created; the 990 address is Antwerp. The company's website returned no readable content.

Cole's Coatings' own site says it is a powder coating, sand blasting and chemical stripping shop in Hillsboro, Ohio, which matches the Highland County project in JobsOhio's October 2024 report: a $25,000 Small Business Grant for a $73,800 investment creating one job. The 990 gives a Winchester mailing address in the same corner of the state.

JobsOhio's October 2024 report lists a $25,000 Small Business Grant in financial services for a Portage County project with eight jobs retained, one created and no capital investment, which fits a professional services firm at the Kent address on the 990. A site at escottco.com describes a sales-compensation consulting practice run by Elliot Scott but does not state a location, so I did not rely on it.

Ice Barrel's own site sells cold-water-therapy barrels and chillers direct to consumers. JobsOhio's August 2024 report lists a $25,000 Small Business Grant in advanced manufacturing for a $70,000 project across Ashland and Holmes counties with four jobs retained and two created; the 990 address is Sugarcreek. Nothing in any source points to a parent company.

parent: Miami Valley Metal Investment Group LLC
notes: The name reads like a holding company, but JobsOhio classes the project as advanced manufacturing and lists seven jobs retained and two created on a $39,000 investment with a $25,000 Inclusion Grant, so the recipient is a small operating metal business in Dayton rather than a real-estate vehicle. No website or news coverage was found.

OhioSE describes Plastic Compounders as a multi-generational family-owned recycler of post-industrial plastic that has employed local residents in Cambridge since 1965; the $25,000 Small Business Grant added an eighth extrusion line. The August 2024 JobsOhio report lists 22 jobs retained and five created on a $500,000 investment, and the Small Business Grant itself is restricted to small businesses.

JobsOhio classes this Putnam County project as advanced manufacturing, not construction or real estate, with a $25,000 Small Business Grant, $50,690 invested, one job retained and one created, so it is treated as a small operating business at the Holgate address on the 990. The similarly named Schwab Builders Inc. whose site covers San Francisco Bay Area home building is a different firm. Graded C because the industry label is the only thing describing what the company does.

The company's own site describes stainless steel and mild steel fabrication, certified welding, CNC plasma cutting and press brake work. JobsOhio's June 2023 report lists a $50,000 Inclusion Grant in advanced manufacturing with one job retained and five created on a $320,000 investment; the county field in that row is garbled by the PDF layout, and the 990 address is Sandusky in Erie County.

JobsOhio's October 2024 report lists a $50,000 Small Business Grant in the technology sector for a Sandusky County project with 13 jobs retained, two created and no capital investment, which matches a small security firm at the Fremont address on the 990. The Fremont News-Messenger has covered Kuns Northcoast Security and its president, but its articles are paywalled and I could not fetch one.

JobsOhio's October 2024 report lists a $50,000 Small Business Grant in aerospace and aviation for a Wood County project with 28 jobs retained and five created and no capital investment; the 990 address is Bowling Green. The Fabricator reported in 2019 that Clark Fixture opened a facility in Mexico, so the company is not Ohio-only, but the Small Business Grant's size limits and the 28 retained jobs keep it under 100. I could not fetch The Fabricator article.
